import pytest
from your_module import is_valid_email


class TestIsValidEmail:
    """Test suite for is_valid_email function."""

    # ========== Happy Path Tests ==========
    
    @pytest.mark.parametrize("email", [
        "user@example.com",
        "john.doe@example.com",
        "jane_doe@example.org",
        "user-name@example.co.uk",
        "user+tag@example.com",
        "user%123@example.com",
        "user@subdomain.example.com",
        "user@example-domain.com",
        "a@b.com",
        "very.common@example.com",
        "disposable.style.email.with+symbol@example.com",
        "other.email-with-hyphen@example.com",
        "fully-qualified-domain@example.com",
        "user.name+tag+sorting@example.com",
        "x@example.com",
        "example-indeed@strange-example.com",
        "test.email@123.123.123.123",
        "email@domain-one.com",
        "_______@example.com",
        "firstname+lastname@example.com",
    ])
    def test_valid_emails(self, email):
        """Test that valid email formats return True."""
        assert is_valid_email(email) is True

    # ========== Edge Cases ==========
    
    @pytest.mark.parametrize("email", [
        "user@example.museum",          # Long TLD
        "user@example.travel",          # 6-char TLD
        "user@example.photography",     # Very long TLD
        "user@example.xn--p1ai",        # Internationalized domain (punycode)
        "user@123.456.789.0",           # IP-like domain
        "user@[192.168.1.1]",           # IP literal (should fail but edge case)
        "UPPERCASE@EXAMPLE.COM",        # All uppercase
        "MixedCase@Example.Com",        # Mixed case
        "user@localhost",               # Local hostname (no TLD)
        "user@example.c",               # Single character TLD
        "user@example.1",               # Numeric TLD
        "user@example.a1",              # Alphanumeric TLD
        "user@example.12",              # Two-digit TLD
        "user@example.123",             # Three-digit TLD
        "user@example.a" * 10,          # Very long email
        "a" * 64 + "@example.com",      # Long local part
        "user@" + "a" * 63 + ".com",    # Long domain part
    ])
    def test_edge_case_emails(self, email):
        """Test edge case email formats."""
        # These may or may not be valid depending on strictness
        # Document the behavior rather than asserting specific outcomes
        result = is_valid_email(email)
        assert isinstance(result, bool)

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("email,expected", [
        ("user@example.com", True),     # Standard valid
        ("", False),                     # Empty string
        (" ", False),                    # Whitespace only
        ("\t\n", False),                # Whitespace characters
        (" user@example.com ", False),  # Leading/trailing spaces
        ("user@example.com\n", False),  # Newline at end
    ])
    def test_whitespace_handling(self, email, expected):
        """Test handling of whitespace in emails."""
        assert is_valid_email(email) == expected
